name: InfinityFree
tagline: 100% free web hosting forever — no paid tiers, no ads on your site
description: InfinityFree is a genuinely free-forever web hosting provider offering 5GB storage, unlimited bandwidth (capped by hit limits) and no ads on hosted sites.
about: InfinityFree is run by iFastNet and stands out from most "free hosting" providers by not gating any paid tier behind the free plan — there's exactly one plan, it costs nothing, and it doesn't place ads on the websites it hosts. Accounts get 5GB of disk space, up to 30,000 files (inodes), a 10MB per-file size cap, and 400 MySQL databases, with PHP 8.3 and MariaDB support alongside a Softaculous installer for WordPress and 400+ other scripts.

"Unlimited bandwidth" on the free plan is not unlimited traffic — InfinityFree enforces a rolling cap of roughly 50,000 "hits" per 24 hours, where every image, script, stylesheet and page load counts as a separate hit. In practice that works out to somewhere around 100-300 real visitors a day for a typical WordPress site before the account gets rate-limited or temporarily suspended. There is no email hosting on the free plan at all — no @yourdomain.com inboxes — so anyone who needs business email has to pair it with a separate provider or upgrade to iFastNet's paid hosting.

Because it's free, InfinityFree carries no uptime SLA and no guaranteed support response time. Help is handled through a community support forum rather than live chat or phone, and free accounts can be suspended for inactivity or for exceeding resource limits. It's a solid way to test a site, learn web development or run a genuinely low-traffic personal project — not a dependable home for a business site that needs guaranteed uptime, fast support or built-in email.
policies: InfinityFree charges nothing for its hosting plan, so there is no billing, no refund process and no money-back guarantee to speak of — there's simply no payment to refund.

Free accounts are subject to fair-use enforcement: sites that exceed the daily hit limit, disk quota or file-count cap can be rate-limited or suspended, and accounts left inactive for an extended period may be reclaimed. Review InfinityFree's terms of service on its own site before relying on it for anything business-critical.
